newsitem.title: USA: Staying or going? List of key Clinton personnel.
newsitem.headline: Staying or going? List of key Clinton personnel.

text.p: The following is a list of cabinet secretaries, department directors and other key officials of President Bill Clinton's administration and their likely status in the second term.

-- White House Chief of Staff Leon Panetta: is leaving to return to California where the former congressman may run for governor. Erskine Bowles, a North Carolina businessman and longtime Clinton friend, is reported to be a strong candidate to replace Panetta.

-- Secretary of State Warren Christopher: announced his resignation on Thursday. U.N. Ambassador Madeleine Albright and former Senate Majority Leader George Mitchell are considered leading candidates to succeed him.

-- Defence Secretary William Perry: has told the president he will resign. CIA Director John Deutch reported to be a strong candidate to replace him. Others mentioned are deputy defence secretary John White, Republican Sen. Richard Lugar of Indiana and former Democratic Sen. Sam Nunn of Georgia.
-- Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin: Is expected to remain in his current position.
-- Attorney General Janet Reno: repeated Thursday she wants to remain in office if asked by Clinton and said no one at the White House had ever directly criticised her performance.

-- Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor: a spokesman said on Wednesday that Kantor was planning to return to private life. Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky has been mentioned as a possible replacement.

-- Acting Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky: could be formally nominated to keep the Trade job, but potential problem is that she once represented Canada and Quebec in a lumber dispute. A law bars anyone who has worked for a foreign government in a trade dispute with the United States from the Trade job. Barshefsky has been mentioned as a possible Cmmerce or Transportation Secretary.
-- Labour Secretary Robert Reich: officials say Reich has not decided whether he will stay, but he is rumoured to be considering moving back to Boston for family reasons.
-- Transportation Secretary Federico Pena: gave resignation to Clinton on Thursday.
-- Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman: has said he would like to remain as agriculture secretary and there are no signs Clinton wants him to leave.

-- Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary: has spent the last two years under siege and confirmed on Wednesday that she was resigning. Rumoured replacements include Deputy Secretary Charles Curtis and Representative Bill Richardson, a New Mexico Democrat.
-- Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala: expected to keep her post.
-- Housing and Urban Development Secretary Henry Cisneros: reported to be leaving but has said his status has not been decided.
-- Education Secretary Richard Riley: has not made any decision about whether he will stay, his press secretary said.
-- Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt: has said he plans to remain in his current post.

-- National Economic Council head Laura Tyson: administration officials are speculating that Tyson will leave. Tyson's office declined to comment, but reports indicate Tyson's husband and son have already moved back to California.
-- White House adviser George Stephanopoulos: has said he expects to leave after taking "a week to think about it on the beach."
-- Environmental Protection Agency Director Carol Browner: plans to stay on the job, which is not a cabinet-level post.
-- Office of Management and Budget Director Franklin Raines: a recent appointee, Raines is expected to remain.
-- Securities and Exchange Commission Chairman Arthur Levitt: plans to stay in the next administration, an SEC public affairs staff member said.
-- Food and Drug Administration Director David Kessler: an appointee under former President George Bush, expected to stay on to spearhead the anti-smoking campaign.
